title: Vendor Verification Checklist & Weighted Evaluation Rubric When Cleaning Quotes Vary by 50%
seoTitle: Weighted Evaluation Rubric: Why Cleaning Quotes Vary by 50 Percent
metaDescription: Use a weighted evaluation rubric when cleaning quotes vary by 50%: score ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hr labor math, W-2 COI limits, and compare bids in our calculator.
excerpt: When commercial cleaning bids span a 50% price spread, awarding the contract based on bottom-line price alone sets up a 90-day re-bid cycle. Use this 100-point weighted evaluation rubric and vendor verification scorecard to grade production rate realism, W-2 labor compliance, and scope completeness objectively.
quickAnswer: A weighted evaluation rubric resolves why cleaning quotes vary by 50 percent by grading proposals across five objective categories totaling 100 points: Labor Hour & ISSA 3,500 Sq Ft/Hr Realism (30 points), Scope Completeness & Normalized Pricing ($0.07–$0.15/sq ft depending on bracket, 25 points), W-2 Statutory Insurance & OSHA Compliance (20 points), Quality Control & Supervision Ratios (15 points), and On-Site Material Handling Equipment (10 points). Any bidder scoring below 75/100 or failing W-2 Workers' Compensation verification should be disqualified regardless of price.

blocks.text: When three commercial cleaning vendors submit monthly quotes of $2,100, $2,950, and $4,200 for the exact same office suite, procurement teams often split into two camps: finance pushes for the $2,100 bid to hit quarterly OPEX targets, while operations fears the cheapest vendor will abandon daily vacuuming and restroom detailing within 30 days. Bridging that conflict requires replacing subjective gut impressions with a quantitative weighted evaluation rubric designed specifically to unpack why cleaning quotes vary by 50 percent.
1. The 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Janitorial Proposals

In commercial facility procurement, price should account for no more than 25% of the total evaluation score—and only after every proposal has been normalized for identical square footage, visit frequency (using the 4.33 weeks/month standard), and add-on scope. The remaining 75 points measure whether the contractor has allocated sufficient labor hours, legal W-2 workforce protection, supervisory oversight, and commercial equipment to execute the contract.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Comparing Divergent Commercial Cleaning Bids
rows: 1. Labor Hours & ISSA Production Realism (30 Pts)
Implied rate >4,800 sq ft/hr; hides nightly hours; ignores 1.12x tile/grout burden
3,500–4,000 sq ft/hr; discloses nightly crew hours & 4.33 wk/mo visit math
2,800–3,500 sq ft/hr tailored to flooring mix (1.0x–1.12x) & restroom density
2. Normalized Price & Scope Parity (25 Pts)
More than 25% below market ($35/hr W-2 floor) or >30% above benchmark without extra scope
Within regional $/sq ft bracket ($0.07–$0.12 for 10k–25k sq ft); add-ons itemized
Transparent line-item pricing: base labor, restrooms ($15–$30), breakrooms ($12–$25), consumables
3. W-2 Compliance, COI & OSHA Safety (20 Pts)
Uses 1099 cash crews; missing Class 9014 Workers' Comp or <$1M General Liability
100% W-2 staff; $1M/$2M GL + statutory WC + $25k janitorial dishonesty bond
W-2 verified, E-Verify, $5M Umbrella, site-specific OSHA HazCom & Bloodborne logs
4. Supervision, QA & Turnover Control (15 Pts)
No dedicated field supervisor; >120% annual turnover; no formal inspection log
Biweekly supervisor inspection; <75% turnover; 24-hour deficiency response SLA
Weekly GPS-stamped digital QA audits; dedicated night lead; backup floater crew within 2 hrs
5. Commercial Equipment & Ergonomics (10 Pts)
Residential vacuums, string mops, unvented barrels causing slow trash pulls
Commercial HEPA vacuums, color-coded microfiber, standard rolling bins
CRI-certified HEPA backpacks, OSHA step-on medical bins, high-capacity rolling collectors

blocks.text: 2. Scoring Category 1 (30 Points): Labor Hour & Production Rate Verification

Because direct labor accounts for 70% to 78% of a commercial cleaning contract, 30 out of 100 rubric points belong to production rate verification. Take your facility's cleanable usable square footage (USF) and divide it by the bidder's proposed nightly labor hours. Compare that figure against the ISSA benchmark of 3,500 square feet per hour, adjusted for your flooring and fixture density.

For example, in a 20,000-square-foot suite with mixed carpet and hard flooring (1.05x multiplier), six ceramic-tile restrooms (1.12x multiplier, $15–$30 per restroom per visit), and two busy breakrooms ($12–$25 per visit), the effective target production rate is roughly 3,100 to 3,400 sq ft/hr—requiring 5.9 to 6.5 labor hours per night (127.7 to 140.7 hours per month at 5x/week / 21.65 visits). Award the full 30 points to bidders proposing 5.8 to 6.6 nightly hours. Deduct 15 points if a bidder proposes 4.0 to 4.5 hours, and award 0 points (mandatory disqualification) if a bidder claims they can clean the suite in 3.2 hours (6,250 sq ft/hr).

blocks.title: The Minimum Implied Hourly Wage Floor Test
blocks.text: After verifying monthly labor hours, subtract any bundled consumables ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) or amortized floor care ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/month) from the monthly price and divide the remainder by total monthly labor hours. If the resulting hourly billing rate is below $35/hour (the national baseline for compliant W-2 commercial janitorial labor, ranging from $35 to $65/hr), the vendor cannot legally cover prevailing cleaner wages, payroll taxes, and workers' compensation.
3. Scoring Category 2 & 3 (45 Points Combined): Normalized Price Parity & Mandatory Pass/Fail Compliance

To score the 25-point Normalized Price & Scope Parity section fairly, strip out optional add-ons or add standardized allowances so every vendor is judged on the exact same deliverables. Verify that their normalized rate per square foot falls inside your size bracket's healthy band—adjusted by the frequency multiplier (1.08x for 1x/week, 1.00x for 2x/week, 0.95x for 3x/week, or 0.90x for 5x/week):

items: Under 2,500 sq ft: $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit (subject to a $90 to $135 minimum trip charge per visit).
2,500 – 9,999 sq ft: $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit.
10,000 – 24,999 sq ft: $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft per visit.
25,000+ sq ft: $0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft per visit.

blocks.text: Next, grade the 20-point W-2 Compliance, Insurance & OSHA section as both a point score and a strict gating criterion. Require every finalist to submit a specimen Certificate of Insurance (COI), their Workers' Compensation Experience Modification Rate (EMR—ideally under 1.00), proof of a third-party Fidelity/Janitorial Dishonesty Bond, and their OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binder protocol.
4. Scoring Category 4 & 5 (25 Points Combined): Supervision Systems & Waste-Collection Hardware

Why do two W-2 contractors paying identical wages still submit quotes that vary by 25%? Frequently, the difference lies in their material-handling efficiency and supervisory infrastructure. A well-capitalized contractor invests in commercial waste-collection hardware that shaves 30 to 45 minutes off nightly trash pulls in multi-floor or large-footprint suites, letting them pass real labor savings back to the client without rushing restroom sanitation.

blocks.title: Equipment Specs That Justify a Higher Efficiency Score
blocks.text: During your vendor verification check, award the full 10 equipment points to bidders who deploy purpose-built waste and clinical hardware rather than dragging unmounted barrels across your floors. Mounting 20-to-55-gallon barrels onto a Rubbermaid Commercial Brute 5-Caster Trash Can Dolly (twist-lock base rated to 250 lb capacity with 5 quiet swivel casters) prevents floor scuffing and back strain. For large suites or multi-floor evening trash pulls, a Rubbermaid Commercial Mega BRUTE Mobile Collector 120-Gal (400 lb weight capacity, 12-inch non-marking wheels, and rear sortation doors) consolidates waste collection into a single elevator trip. In wellness rooms, first-aid stations, or clinical suites, verify compliance with a Rubbermaid Commercial Slim Jim Step-On Front-Step 18-Gallon Bin featuring a hands-free foot pedal, quiet internal-hinge lid, and OSHA/medical compliance.
5. 4-Step Execution Workflow to Run Your Vendor Scorecard

items.name: Issue a Mandatory Bid Breakdown Sheet Before the Walkthrough
items.text: Refuse single-line lump-sum PDFs. Require bidders to fill in your 7-line form showing cleanable USF, nightly labor hours, implied $/hr rate, 4.33-week monthly visit total, restroom line item, breakroom/glass line item, and consumable option.

items.name: Run the Pass/Fail Gate on W-2 Status and Implied Hourly Floor
items.text: Eliminate any bidder utilizing 1099 sub-crews or quoting an implied labor rate below $35/hour before your committee scores the proposals.

items.name: Have Three Stakeholders Score Finalists Independently on the 100-Point Rubric
items.text: Have Facility Operations, Procurement/Finance, and Office Administration grade each proposal across all five categories, then average the scores.

items.name: Conduct a 15-Minute Post-Score Reference & Supervisor Interview
items.text: For the top-scoring vendor (typically scoring 82 to 94 points), interview the exact regional field supervisor assigned to your building and call two current tenants of comparable square footage.

faqs.q: Why does our weighted rubric allocate more points to labor hours (30 pts) than price (25 pts)?
faqs.a: In commercial janitorial services, price is directly derivative of labor hours. If a vendor under-allocates nightly hours by 40% to win a price-weighted bid, your facility simply receives 40% less cleaning—leading to overflowing breakrooms, unvacuumed carpet traffic lanes, and contract termination within 90 days. Weighting labor realism at 30 points ensures you only compare prices among vendors proposing viable staffing levels.

faqs.q: What is an acceptable annual employee turnover rate when scoring janitorial vendors?
faqs.a: While the broader retail and low-tier janitorial industry suffers turnover rates exceeding 150% to 200% annually, best-in-class commercial building service contractors maintain annual turnover below 50% to 75% by paying competitive W-2 wages, assigning full-shift routes, and providing ergonomic equipment.

faqs.q: How do we score a proposal that bundles quarterly carpet extraction and VCT waxing?
faqs.a: Unbundle it before scoring Category 2. Standard amortized deep floor care runs $0.03 to $0.06 per square foot per month ($450 to $900/month for a 15,000 sq ft office). Subtract that line item from the turnkey bidder's monthly total so you can compare routine nightly cleaning labor apples-to-apples against vendors who quoted floor care as an optional add-on.

faqs.q: What insurance endorsements should be mandatory pass/fail items on our checklist?
faqs.a: Require four non-negotiable items on the Certificate of Insurance: (1) Commercial General Liability of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate naming your company and landlord as Additional Insured; (2) Statutory W-2 Workers' Compensation (Class Code 9014); (3) a Waiver of Subrogation; and (4) a $25,000 to $100,000 Third-Party Employee Dishonesty (Janitorial) Bond.
